First, we'll adopt Thomas's phased approach. Phase one will address the voluntary-disclosure eligibility requirements now — identifying model v4.2 and including the non-waiver statement preserving applicable privilege. Phase two will incorporate the validated impact numbers and remediation figures once Nadia's independent validation is complete.

Second, on customer-impact numbers — I agree with Nadia. We will not lock in specific figures until the independent validation is finished. The audited amount the client has authorized for refunds will be the validated amount, not the draft. Nadia, please coordinate directly with the validation team to get us a turnaround estimate as soon as possible so we can assess whether we'll be ready for next month's meeting or need to request a brief extension.

Third, on response posture — we will provide a factual description of how the pricing system operates, as the regulator has requested, without characterizing our conduct as wrongful or admitting liability. This aligns with the client's position as communicated by Michael.

Fourth, customer identifiers submitted to the regulator will be handled under a confidential-treatment request, built into the plan for whenever those details are submitted.

Fifth, Michael, please get your call notes into the investigation file promptly so we have documentation of the client's position.

I'll hold off on formally settling the plan until we have the validation timeline, but these are the parameters I'm approving. Are there any objections before I finalize?

No encoding fix is needed for C4 or C5 since they pass whenever PF2 is revealed. For C1, no check-wording change is needed in isolation because C1 passes in all three rollouts where PF2 is also revealed; the C1 failure in rollout 2 is a downstream consequence of PF2 not being revealed, not an independent encoding mismatch.
